biography.plain_text: Sune Tamm was a Swedish naval officer, merchant captain and maritime educator. After commanding torpedo boats, he trained future officers at the Rydberg Foundation and later managed shipping for industrial companies. He also served as director of Lundsberg School, his former school, and chaired the Nautical Society in Gothenburg for many years.

long_biography.plain_text:
Maritime educator Sune Tamm arranged the purchase of a larger training ship in San Francisco for the Rydberg Foundation. He commanded its delivery voyage around Cape Horn to Sweden, where it replaced the foundation's smaller vessel. His subsequent training voyages gave prospective officers experience aboard a working sailing ship.

His navigational expertise also found an unusual application in Sweden's new translation of the New Testament. For the Bible commission, he examined the account of the storm encountered by the apostle Paul's ship near Crete. Tamm calculated the vessel's likely speed and the measures its crew must have taken.
